KEY MESSAGE 1...The remnants of Isaias will continue to bring 
rains and a few thunderstorms to the region overnight. 

A low pressure system which was formerly Isaias is slowly weakening
while moving NE across the western NC/VA areas this afternoon 
and it will continue NE across the Middle Atlantic areas overnight.
The first large area of rains ahead of the system is moving NE 
across the PA/NJ areas while a back edge of steady rains is 
trailing across ern MD/DE. Scattered showers in this area will 
fill in after sunset as more dynamics arrive and limited instability
develops too. While there is a chance for a few TSTMs across 
the area this evening, most spots will not have one. Delmarva 
and south NJ are the areas most likely to have some thunder. 
Winds will continue to be East or Northeast for most areas today
and tonight. As the low moves by late tonight winds could turn 
South across SE Delaware near where the low passes by. 

A soaking rain has already occurred, but more overnight will
bring storm total rains up into the 1 to 2 inch range for most
areas. The rains (so far) have occurred at a rate which has
limited any significant flooding and we expect that this will be
the case overnight too. Limited ponding on roads and other minor
flooding can be expected however. WPC has maintained most of 
the region in a Marginal Risk (level 1 out of 4) for excessive 
rainfall into tonight, which means isolated instances of flash 
flooding will be possible.  

After the rains end tonight, we can expect a continuation of low
clouds and fog thru dawn. Lower VSBYS in fog may cause some
travel concerns for the morning commute. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Widespread minor tidal flooding expected Monday
morning for much of the Atlantic Ocean coasts in New Jersey and
Delaware.

While we will be moving away from the New Moon, and winds will 
begin to turn with the passage of the remnant low, tidal levels
will remain elevated Monday morning as winds will remain shore
parallel in many locations. This will trap water along the
coast, and particularly in the back bays, resulting in a round 
of widespread minor tidal flooding across most of the Atlantic 
Ocean coast in New Jersey and Delaware as well as along the 
Delaware Bay shore in Kent County, Delaware. 

Spotty minor tidal flooding is also possible Monday morning 
along the remainder of the Delaware Bay coasts, the tidal 
Delaware River, the Raritan Bay coast, and the Atlantic Ocean 
coast in Monmouth County. 

No tidal flooding concerns expected along the Chesapeake Bay.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Increasing temperatures and humid conditions through 
midweek with some shower chances. The pattern becomes more active 
towards the end of the week and into the start of the weekend. By 
the weekend, temperatures get much cooler.

An expansive mid and upper-level ridge well to our south will keep 
the flow more zonal through much of this coming week. There will be 
multiple pieces of upper-level energy moving through the region 
along with a cold front leading to some shower chances this week. A 
cold front sinks south into the area Tuesday night and into 
Wednesday as a mid-level shortwave also moves through the region. 
This may lead to some isolated showers Tuesday evening into Tuesday 
night. However, any precipitation currently looks limited. The cold 
front may not fully clear our area until later in the day Wednesday. 
Additional isolated showers are possible Wednesday evening into 
Wednesday night as more upper-level energy moves through the region. 
By Thursday, it is drier as high pressure builds in. In terms of 
temperatures, on Tuesday highs reach the 70s for many with humid 
conditions. On Wednesday, highs mainly reach the mid 70s to mid 80s 
with humid conditions continuing. Behind the cold front, highs on 
Thursday are in the 60s for most with lower humidity values.

By Thursday night, the upper-level pattern begins to become more 
amplified. An upper-level trough approaches the region from the west 
for the end of the week and moves into the Northeast this weekend. 
There is a large amount of variation among model guidance given this 
being towards the end of the long term period. As of right now, at 
the surface, a deepening low pressure system in Canada will continue 
to move eastward as it strengthens. This low pressure system 
currently looks to bring rain to the area during the time period of 
Thursday night through Friday night. A strong cold front looks to 
move through sometime Friday leading to much cooler conditions this 
weekend. Right now, highs on Friday are mainly in the low 60s to low 
70s. Over the weekend, forecast highs are mainly in the 50s. It will 
also be a windy period due to the deepening low to the north and an 
expansive high building in from the west leading to a tight pressure 
gradient across the region.
